name: Crucible Furnace Floor Safety Coverall
description: Standard-issue for Crucible smelting and foundry floor workers in non-supervisory roles, this coverall is built for sustained high-heat environments. The outer shell is a ceramic-fiber reinforced Nomex equivalent in Crucible's standard burnt-orange safety color, with reflective silver tape at the ankles, wrists, and shoulders. Interior lining is a moisture-wicking thermal buffer that manages heat stress for up to four hours of continuous furnace-proximity work. Tool loops run along both thighs, and a reinforced patch pocket at the chest accommodates standard Crucible-issued rad dosimeters. Tail accommodation is achieved through a rear zip panel from the waist down. Chrome arm and shoulder ports are accessible via hook-and-loop flap covers rated to 400°C surface contact.
cultural_context: Every Crucible foundry worker knows this coverall. It's practical, uncomfortable in the upper chest, and smells of metal and sweat after the first week of use. Workers often write their names inside the collar in permanent marker because the laundering system loses them constantly. Wearing it outside work is rare but happens — it signals a kind of hard-labor dignity that some people wear with pride.
story_hooks: A batch of coveralls is distributed with defective thermal buffers — the failure mode isn't obvious until someone is already in danger.
A worker is found wearing a coverall with a falsified Crucible employee ID sewn in, gaining access to restricted smelting floor areas for reasons unknown.
The rad dosimeters issued with this coverall have been quietly recalibrated to underreport exposure, and workers are getting sick.
related_entities: TESSERA CORPONATION Aegis CorpSec Hardened Security BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body coverall with aggressive safety engineering—burnt-orange fabric dominates with silver reflective striping at pressure points. The silhouette is boxy and functional, designed for layering protective gear underneath. Visible hardware and flap-covered ports give it an industrial, almost tactical appearance. The rear zip panel creates a subtle vertical accent line down the back.
physical_description.fit: Loose and relaxed through the torso to accommodate thermal undergarments and movement in extreme heat. Tapered slightly at wrists and ankles for closure precision. Reinforced shoulder and upper-chest panels create mild bunching—intentional, not flattering. Designed for someone wearing augmented chrome limbs without restriction.
physical_description.primary_material: Ceramic-fiber reinforced Nomex equivalent (syntho-aramid blend), exterior rated to 400°C radiant heat. Interior lined with moisture-wicking thermal buffer fabric, slightly translucent in places where heat stress management is critical.
physical_description.texture: Outer shell has a subtle waffle-weave texture for heat dissipation. Seams are heavily stitched and visible. Reflective tape has a raised, almost gritty tactile quality. Flap covers over ports are soft hook-and-loop, contrast against the rigid main fabric. Interior lining is smooth, almost gel-like.
physical_description.color_scheme: Crucible standard burnt-orange (Pantone 158C equivalent) dominates. Reflective silver-gray striping at both wrists, both ankles, and both shoulders in 5cm bands. Chest pocket has faded, individual-marked creasing. Chrome ports visible as dark metallic rectangles with orange fabric underneath.
physical_description.closures: Full-length front zipper (industrial YKK-equivalent, rated 300°C). Rear waist-to-ankle zip panel. Wrist and ankle closures are friction-fit elastic with velcro overlap. Chest pocket has a simple snap closure. Port covers secured with heavy-duty hook-and-loop rated for thermal cycling.
distinctive_features: Chrome-rated arm and shoulder ports with removable flap covers—designed for integrated augmentation access
Reinforced chest patch pocket for rad dosimeter mounting (faint circular wear stain visible)
Rear full-length zip panel for tail accommodation—visible from behind as an orange rectangular accent
Tool loops on both thighs (often have ghost marks from keys, cutting tools, wear patterns)
Handwritten name inside collar in faded permanent marker—personal ID marker indicating laundering casualty risk
Asymmetrical wear patterns on shoulders and forearms from repetitive foundry work
Small burn scars and minor discoloration on lower sleeves (normal operating condition)
Thermal buffer interior visible at collar and cuffs—slightly glossy, heat-resistant finish
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3. This is issued corporate workwear, not salvage. The precision engineering and thermal rating indicate corporate investment in worker safety (liability protection). However, the utilitarian brutalism signals working-class labor, not desk-tier comfort. Visible wear and personal marking humanize what is otherwise standardized corporate equipment.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by Crucible foundry workers—non-supervisory roles handling molten metal and high-heat processes. Signals honest industrial labor, heat-resistant competence, and loyalty to one of the GLMZ's largest manufacturing operations. Wearing it off-shift occasionally carries connotations of working-class pride or exhaustion—a uniform you can't shake off. Augmented workers prefer this garment because the port access is engineered specifically for chrome limbs, making it more accessible to cyborged laborers than standard apparel.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in after first month. Thermal discoloration develops around the chest and shoulders. Collar becomes soft and worn. Handwritten name fades but remains legible. Minor scuff marks and burn damage accumulate—considered normal operating condition, not damage. The garment doesn't age badly; it just becomes more 'lived-in.' Smell of metal and sweat is permanent after week two.
